proposition: Let a_0 = 6, a_1 = 16 and a_n = 5*a_(n-1) + (-6)*a_(n-2) for n >= 2. Then for every n with 0 <= n <= 25, a_n = 3*2^n + 4*3^n.
hypotheses: the recurrence is applied only for n >= 2

argument.text: For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 25, n^2 + 1 exceeds n.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 25, if n mod 2 = 1 then (n^2) mod 2 = 1.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 25, (n-4)*(n^2) equals (n-4)*((n^2) + [n = 4]).
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 25, if n mod 4 = 0 then (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 25, at least one of the following holds: n mod 3 = 0; n mod 3 = 1; n mod 3 = 2.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 25, at least one of the following holds: n mod 3 = 0; n mod 3 = 1; n mod 3 = 2.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 25, n*(n+1) is congruent to (n*(n+1)) + 437 modulo 23.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 25 for which n^3 > 12.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 25, (n-3)*(n^2) equals (n-3)*((n^2) + [n = 3]).
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 25 for which n^2 > 25.
For every integer n with 2 <= n <= 25, n^3 is at least 3*n.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 25, n*(n+1) is congruent to (n*(n+1)) + 561 modulo 3.
The steps above establish the statement up to 25, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 25.
